newsitem.title: UK: Sibneft first Russian corporate to set public bond.
newsitem.headline: Sibneft first Russian corporate to set public bond.

text.p: A.O. Siberian Oil Company (Sibneft) on Friday became the first Russian corporate to issue a public Eurobond.
The $125 million three-year floating-rate note was priced to yield four percentage points over Libor.
Salomon Brothers underwrote the transaction, and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Dresdner Kleinwort Benson were part of the syndicate.
"This is the first Russian corporate issuer to publicly access the international debt capital markets," Salomon Brothers said.
In July Russia's biggest oil company NK LUKoil raised $125 million via a privately placed bond. The deal was issued via LUKoil's Dutch subsidiary and had a one-year maturity.
There is a long list of Russian borrowers waiting to raise funds in the Eurobond market.

After Russia's debut dollar deal last November, municipalities and banks have come to the public market, but there had been no corporate borrowers. Among those planning deals are gas giant Gazprom and car makers AvtoVAZ and GAZ.
Sibneft is not rated, but bankers said the pricing of its bond was in line with yields on debt launched by Russian banks.
"In Libor terms, the pricing is in line with where the leading financial borrowers are trading, like Uneximbank and SBS-Agro," a dealer said.
In July SBS-Agro became the first Russian bank to tap the public bond markets, with a $250 million three-year bond. It is rated B1 by Moody's and B plus by Standard & Poor's.
Uneximbank followed with a $200 million three-year bond. It is rated Ba3 by Moody's and BB by S&P.
